message.content:
Below are two ways to spin up a **Compute Engine** instance that has an NVIDIA RTX‑A6000‑style GPU (the closest match in GCP is the **NVIDIA A100** – GCP does not expose an “RTX A6000” SKU) and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

> **Prerequisites**  
> * You have a Google Cloud project with billing enabled.  
> * The **Compute Engine API** is enabled (`gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com`).  
> * You have the **gcloud CLI** installed and authenticated (`gcloud auth login`).  
> * You have a GPU quota in the zone you plan to use (e.g., `nvidia-tesla-a100` in `us-central1-a`).  

---

## 1.  gcloud CLI command

```bash
# Variables
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"          # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-tesla-a100"          # closest to RTX A6000
GPU_COUNT=1
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
  --accelerator="type=$GPU_TYPE,count=$GPU_COUNT" \
  --image-family="$IMAGE_FAMILY" \
  --image-project="$IMAGE_PROJECT" \
  --boot-disk-size=200GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
  --tags=http-server,https-server
```

* `--metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh` – optional, if you want to run a script on first boot (e.g., install CUDA drivers).  
* `--tags=http-server,https-server` – opens ports 80/443 if you plan to host a web service.  

**Tip:** If you need more GPUs, increase `GPU_COUNT` and adjust the machine type accordingly (e.g., `n1-highmem-32`).

---

## 2.  REST API (JSON body)

If you prefer to call the Compute Engine REST API directly (e.g., from a CI/CD pipeline), use the following POST request:

```http
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{PROJECT}/zones/{ZONE}/instances
Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_OAUTH_TOKEN>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "zones/{ZONE}/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 200,
        "diskType": "zones/{ZONE}/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/{PROJECT}/zones/{ZONE}/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a100",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y cuda-drivers"
      }
    ]
  },
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  }
}
```

### How to get the OAuth token

```bash
gcloud auth application-default print-access-token
```

Replace `{PROJECT}` and `{ZONE}` with your actual project ID and zone. The token returned by the command above can be used in the `Authorization` header.

---

## 3.  Quick sanity check

After the instance is created, you can verify the GPU is visible:

```bash
gcloud compute ssh rtx-a6000-ubuntu --zone=us-central1-a --command="nvidia-smi"
```

You should see an NVIDIA A100 (or the GPU you requested) listed.

---

### What if you really need an RTX A6000?

Google Cloud does **not** offer an RTX A6000 SKU. The closest GPU types are:

| GCP GPU SKU | Approx. CUDA cores | Approx. VRAM |
|-------------|--------------------|--------------|
| nvidia-tesla-a100 | 6912 | 40 GB |
| nvidia-tesla-v100 | 5120 | 16 GB |

If you absolutely must use an RTX A6000, you would need to run the instance on a different cloud provider (e.g., AWS EC2 `g4dn.12xlarge` with RTX A6000) or on-premises hardware.

---

**Happy computing!**
